case: H. J. Heinz Company / Berkshire Hathaway & 3G Capital (2013)

claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; asset retained, merged into Kraft Heinz ~25 months after close; combined-successor ~$15.4bn impairment at ~5.5yr horizon (mostly Kraft-side brands)
claude.rationale: Per section 2, this was a whole-company going-concern take-private in which the product franchise (T4), operating processes/manufacturing/R&D/supply chain (T5), and people/culture (T6) all transferred together intact, so no product-vs-process (gap_45=0) or process-vs-organization (gap_56=0) structural mismatch existed at closing. Section 4 states there was no product-process disruption at the 2013 tier transfer (product and processes moved together intact) → p4_pathway=0, and no process-organization fracture, with operations and people moving together and new management installed → p5_pathway=0. The 2019 impairment is expressly attributed to the combined Kraft Heinz post-2015-merger successor and mainly Kraft-side brands, not the 2013 Heinz asset, so it does not code as a documented 2013-deal pathway.

gemini.performance_metric: non-cash impairment losses of approximately $15.4 billion
gemini.rationale: The dossier states that the product franchise, operating processes, and people all transferred together intact as a going concern, meaning no structural gaps existed at closing (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). At the 3-5 year horizon, the reshaped operating/cost processes under 3G Capital led to an erosion of brand value and a $15.4 billion impairment, indicating a product-process disruption (p4_pathway=1). No fracture between operations and the organization was documented (p5_pathway=0).

grok.performance_metric: no divestiture; retained and merged into Kraft Heinz 2015 (~25 months)
grok.rationale: Section 2 states T4 product franchise and T5 operating processes transferred whole with the going concern; section 5 confirms whole-company take-private with all tiers moving together so no structural gap_45 or gap_56. Section 3 and section 4 explicitly state no product-process disruption or process-organization fracture at the 2013 transfer level (impairments occurred later at combined Kraft Heinz successor). Section 4 codes T1-archetype and T2-model as none documented at 2013 closing.
